editionContext.baseText: Ganjoor online transcription of Ferdowsi’s Shahnameh: the story of Forud, sections 1 to 25.
editionContext.criticalPrintEdition: Not independently established for this online transcription.
editionContext.scope: The story of Forud as the poem tells it: from the army Kay Khosrow sends against Turan under Tus, through the death of Forud at Kalat, to the defeat of the Iranians and the return of Piran; the war of Kamus that follows is not part of it.
editionContext.evidencePolicy: Use actual verse for narrative assertions. Site-generated summaries are not the selected base text.
editionContext.translationPolicy: Original English paraphrases prepared for this collection; not a quoted modern translation.

entities.label: The Shahnameh
entities.summary: The literary work in which the story of Forud is told.

entities.label: Ferdowsi
entities.summary: The poet of the Shahnameh.

entities.label: Forud
entities.summary: The army Kay Khosrow sends against Turan under Tus, and its road past Kalat, where Forud, a son of Siavash, lives with his mother.

entities.label: Kay Khosrow
entities.summary: The young king of Iran, son of Siavash, who seeks vengeance for his father.

entities.label: Tus
entities.summary: A noble of Iran of the line of Nowzar, made commander of the army.

entities.label: Forud
entities.summary: A son of Siavash by the daughter of Piran, who lives in the castle of Kalat with his mother.

entities.label: Siavash
entities.summary: The father of Kay Khosrow and Forud, killed in Turan before this story.

facts.text: Father of Kay Khosrow and Forud

entities.label: Piran
entities.summary: The commander and counsellor of Afrasiab, grandfather of Forud.

entities.label: Rostam
entities.summary: The hero of Iran, who stays at court with the king.

entities.label: Afrasiab
entities.summary: The king of Turan, grandfather of Kay Khosrow and the killer of Siavash.

entities.label: Gudarz
entities.summary: An old noble of Iran, son of Keshvad.

entities.label: Iran
entities.summary: The kingdom of Kay Khosrow.

entities.label: Turan
entities.summary: The kingdom of Afrasiab, where the army is sent.

entities.label: Kalat
entities.summary: A castle on a high mountain beside a narrow road, the home of Forud; the mountain is called Sepid Kuh.

entities.label: Charam
entities.summary: A well-watered land on the road to Kalat, where the army halts.

entities.label: Jarira
entities.summary: The mother of Forud, a daughter of Piran and wife of Siavash.

entities.label: Tokhar
entities.summary: A counsellor of Forud who knows the lords of Iran by name.

entities.label: Bahram son of Gudarz
entities.summary: A warrior of Iran, son of Gudarz, once a companion of Siavash.

facts.text: Warrior of Iran, son of Gudarz

entities.label: Zangeh-ye Shavaran
entities.summary: A warrior of Iran, once a companion of Siavash.

entities.label: Fariborz
entities.summary: A son of Kay Kavus, brother of Siavash and so uncle of Forud.

entities.label: Gostaham
entities.summary: A warrior of Iran, son of Gazhdaham.

entities.label: Bizhan
entities.summary: A young warrior of Iran, the only son of Giv.

facts.text: Warrior of Iran, son of Giv

entities.label: Giv
entities.summary: A warrior of Iran, son of Gudarz, who brought Kay Khosrow from Turan.

entities.label: Rivniz
entities.summary: A young warrior of Iran, son-in-law of Tus.

entities.label: Zarasp
entities.summary: A son of Tus, married to a sister of Rivniz.

entities.label: Rohham
entities.summary: A warrior of Iran, son of Gudarz.

entities.label: Palashan
entities.summary: A young Turanian warrior sent to count the Iranian banners.

entities.label: Tazhav
entities.summary: A Turanian lord of Gorogerd, son-in-law of Afrasiab.

entities.label: Kabudeh
entities.summary: A herdsman of Afrasiab whom Tazhav sends to spy on the Iranians.

entities.label: Espanuy
entities.summary: A woman of the household of Tazhav, called his companion.

entities.label: Kaseh Rud
entities.summary: A river in Turan where the Iranian army makes camp.

entities.label: Gorogerd
entities.summary: The seat of Tazhav, where the herds of Afrasiab graze.

entities.label: Houman
entities.summary: A Turanian hero, brother of Piran.

entities.label: Lahhak
entities.summary: A Turanian warrior.

entities.label: Farshidvard
entities.summary: A Turanian warrior.

entities.label: Rivniz, prince of the house of Kavus
entities.summary: A young crowned prince dear to Kay Kavus; the poem calls him the youngest son of the king. Not the Rivniz who was son-in-law of Tus.

entities.label: Ruyin
entities.summary: A son of Piran.

facts.text: Warrior of Turan, son of Piran

entities.label: Khotan
entities.summary: The land of Piran, to which he returns.

events.label: Tus is given the army
events.summary: Kay Khosrow gives Tus the banner of Kaveh and his seal and makes him commander. He bids him harm no one on the way and not to take the road of Kalat: there lives his brother Forud, a son of Siavash by the daughter of Piran, who knows no one from Iran by name. Tus promises to obey.

events.label: The king and Rostam at court
events.summary: Kay Khosrow returns to his palace and holds a feast with Rostam. He speaks of Afrasiab, of his father’s death and of how he was given to shepherds; Rostam tells him that the world will yet turn to his will.

events.label: Tus chooses the road of Kalat
events.summary: The army reaches a fork: a waterless desert on one side, the road of Kalat and Charam on the other. Tus prefers the green road he once rode. Gudarz reminds him of the king’s order, but Tus dismisses his fear and leads the army towards Kalat.

entityAssociations.role: king whose order is set aside

events.label: Jarira counsels her son
events.summary: Forud hears that the army of Iran is near and drives his herds up the mountain. His mother Jarira tells him that the new king of Iran is his brother: he should put on armour, go before the army and be the first to seek vengeance for Siavash. To know the lords of Iran he should take Tokhar, and ask for Bahram and Zangeh, who were Siavash’s companions.

events.label: Tokhar names the banners
events.summary: Forud and Tokhar ride to a peak above the road and watch thirty thousand riders pass in gold. Tokhar names the lords by their banners: Tus with the elephant, Fariborz the uncle of Forud with the sun, Gostaham with the moon, Zangeh with the wolf, Bizhan son of Giv, Giv, Gudarz with the lion, Rivniz and Bahram son of Gudarz. Forud rejoices at the sight.

events.label: Bahram climbs the mountain
events.summary: Tus sees two riders on the peak and grows angry. He orders a man to find out who they are: an Iranian is to be whipped, a Turk bound or killed, a spy cut in two. Bahram son of Gudarz takes the task and rides up.

events.label: Bahram knows the son of Siavash
events.summary: Bahram calls out roughly, and Forud answers that he should speak gently. Forud asks for Bahram by name; Bahram asks to see the mark of Siavash, and Forud shows a mole on his arm. Bahram bows. Forud offers a week of feasting and to lead the army against Turan, and gives Bahram a mace; Bahram promises to speak to Tus but warns that Tus is headstrong and that any other rider who comes will mean harm.

entityAssociations.role: prince Tus would have had as king

events.label: Tus will not listen
events.summary: Bahram tells Tus that the rider is Forud, whom the king told them not to approach. Tus answers that he commands the army: if the boy is a king, what is he? He calls Forud a Turk’s son blocking the road and mocks Bahram for turning back from a single rider.

events.label: Rivniz falls
events.summary: Tus asks for a man to bring him the head of the Turk. Bahram turns back the first riders by telling them who stands on the mountain, but Rivniz, son-in-law of Tus, rides up alone. Tokhar names him, and Forud’s arrow pins his helmet to his head; he falls dead.

events.label: Zarasp falls
events.summary: Tus sends his own son Zarasp to avenge Rivniz. Tokhar tells Forud who he is, and Forud’s arrow pins him to his saddle. His horse runs back to the army, and Tus puts on his armour and rides against Forud himself.

events.label: Tus returns on foot
events.summary: Tokhar urges Forud to shut himself in the castle, and when he will not, to spare Tus and shoot his horse, since harm to Tus would grieve the king. Forud’s arrow kills the horse; Tus walks back to the camp with his shield on his neck while the women on the walls laugh.

events.label: Giv loses his horse
events.summary: Giv, angered by the shame, puts on armour and rides up. Tokhar tells Forud that Giv brought his brother from Turan and wears the armour of Siavash, which arrows cannot pierce; Forud shoots his horse instead, and Giv too turns back.

events.label: Bizhan swears to go
events.summary: Bizhan reproaches his father for turning back from one rider, and Giv strikes him with his whip. Stung, Bizhan swears not to turn back until he has avenged Zarasp. Gostaham gives him a horse, and Giv, relenting, sends him the armour of Siavash.

events.label: Bizhan fights on foot
events.summary: Tokhar warns that arrows will not pass the armour Bizhan wears. Forud kills his horse, but Bizhan climbs on foot with his sword; another arrow pierces only his shield. Forud turns back to the castle, Bizhan slashes his horse at the gate, and stones from the walls drive him off. Back in camp Tus swears to raze the castle.

events.label: Jarira’s dream
events.summary: At night a thousand men come from Kalat into the castle. Jarira dreams that a fire rises and burns the castle and its people; she wakes, sees the mountain full of armour and spears, and wakes her son. Forud answers that his time has come as his father’s did; he will not ask the Iranians for mercy, and arms his men.

events.label: Forud is struck down
events.summary: Forud rides out with his Turks and fights until noon, until none of them is left. Riding back alone, he is ambushed by Rohham and Bizhan: Rohham strikes his shoulder from behind and Bizhan cuts down his horse. He reaches the castle on foot, the gate is shut, and he dies among the women, his mother at his side.

events.label: Jarira’s end
events.summary: Forud tells the women to throw themselves from the walls rather than be taken by Bizhan, and they do. Jarira burns the treasure, kills the horses in their stable, lays her face on her son’s and takes her own life with a dagger.

events.label: The burial of Forud
events.summary: The Iranians break into the castle. Bahram weeps, saying Forud died more wretchedly than his father, and warns of the king’s anger. Tus comes with Gudarz and Giv and weeps over Forud and his own son; Gudarz rebukes him for his rashness. Tus has a royal tomb built on the mountain, and Forud is laid in it with Zarasp and Rivniz beside him.

events.label: Bizhan and Palashan
events.summary: After three days the army moves on, killing every Turanian it meets, and camps at Kaseh Rud. Palashan comes to count the banners; Bizhan begs Giv to let him go, takes the armour of Siavash, and after a long fight breaks Palashan’s back with his mace and brings his head, horse and armour to Tus.

events.label: Snow at Kaseh Rud
events.summary: Afrasiab orders Piran to gather an army. A cold wind and snow fall on the Iranian camp for a week; tents freeze, men and beasts die and the warriors eat their horses. When the sun returns, Bahram tells Tus that this is the fruit of his war against the son of Siavash; Tus answers that what was written has come to pass.

events.label: Giv burns the mountain of wood
events.summary: Kay Khosrow had charged Giv with burning a mountain of firewood that blocked the road. Bizhan offers to go in his place, but Giv goes himself and sets it alight with an arrow. The fire burns for three weeks; then the army crosses and camps at Gorogerd.

events.label: Bahram and Kabudeh
events.summary: Tazhav, lord of Gorogerd, sends the herdsman Kabudeh by night to spy on the army. Bahram, on watch, hears his horse, shoots him at the belt and, after Kabudeh names Tazhav as his master, cuts off his head.

events.label: Bizhan and Tazhav
events.summary: Tazhav attacks with a small force. Giv offers him gifts if he will come over to Iran, but Tazhav boasts of his crown and herds. Bizhan scorns the offer and charges; the Turanians are cut down, Bizhan snatches Tazhav’s crown from his head and chases him. Tazhav takes Espanuy up behind him, then, his horse failing, sets her down and flees; Bizhan carries her back to Tus.

events.label: Piran gathers the army
events.summary: Tazhav comes weeping to Afrasiab and tells him that Palashan is dead and the land burned. Afrasiab rebukes Piran for his delay; Piran gathers a hundred thousand men and takes a short road to fall on the Iranians unawares. His spies report that the Iranians are drinking day and night with no watch.

events.label: The night attack
events.summary: Piran falls on the camp at midnight with thirty thousand riders. Giv and Gudarz are awake and rouse whom they can, but the drunken army is cut down; at dawn the plain is full of the dead. The survivors flee to a mountain near Kaseh Rud. A rider takes the news to Kay Khosrow, already grieving for his brother, who curses Tus all night.

events.label: Tus in chains
events.summary: Kay Khosrow writes in grief and anger: Tus took the road he forbade and killed his brother. He gives the banner of Kaveh to Fariborz, with Gudarz as counsellor and Giv in the vanguard, and orders Tus home. When Tus kisses the ground before him, the king curses him; only his descent from Manuchehr and his white beard save his head, and he is put in chains.

events.label: A month’s truce
events.summary: Fariborz sends Rohham to Piran: a night attack is not the work of warriors; he may choose war or delay. Piran replies that Tus brought this on himself by killing young and old; he grants a month, after which the Iranians must leave Turan or fight. Fariborz uses the month to equip his army.

events.label: Fariborz flees
events.summary: When the month ends both sides break faith and battle is joined. Gudarz kills nine hundred of Piran’s kin, and Lahhak and Farshidvard charge Giv. Human strikes the centre, Fariborz flees to the mountain and the army breaks. Gudarz turns to flee too, but Giv shames him into standing, and the house of Gudarz swears not to yield.

events.label: The banner cut in two
events.summary: Gudarz sends Bizhan to bring the banner of Kaveh from Fariborz. When Fariborz refuses, Bizhan cuts the banner in two and carries half back, holding off the Turks with arrows. The prince Rivniz is killed, and Bahram lifts his crown from the field on his spear. At nightfall the Iranians withdraw, leaving their wounded; Bizhan takes the unhorsed Gostaham up behind him.

events.label: Bahram goes back for his whip
events.summary: Bahram has lost his whip, with his name on it, while taking the crown. Against the counsel of Gudarz and Giv he rides back by moonlight, finds it among the dead and loses his horse. On foot he holds off a hundred riders and wounds Ruyin son of Piran with his arrows. Piran offers him friendship but no horse; then Tazhav comes with men, and when Bahram is spent, cuts off his arm from behind.

events.label: Giv avenges Bahram
events.summary: Giv and Bizhan find Bahram dying and he names Tazhav. Giv swears revenge, lassos Tazhav from his saddle and drags him back. Bahram asks that Tazhav be spared, but Giv cuts off his head. Bahram dies; Giv builds him a royal tomb, and the army mourns.

events.label: Piran’s triumph
events.summary: The surviving Iranians agree to return to the king and withdraw. Piran finds their camp empty, shares the spoils and sends news to Afrasiab, who meets him with his army and feasts for two weeks. Afrasiab sends him rich gifts and warns him to keep watch: Kay Khosrow is strong, and wherever Rostam leads, no one should sleep easy. Piran returns to Khotan.
